name: 0DTE Day Calendar
summary: Sell the 0DTE option and buy the same strike in the next available expiry; a single-session theta harvest on the steepest part of the decay curve, with a forced same-day close.

legs.strike_rule: Strike by delta: |delta| 0.30-0.45, placed on the side you want to fade, or ATM |delta| ~0.50 for pure pin plays. Must be at least 0.5 x ATR(14 x 5min) away from spot at entry. Put version is the mirror and is preferred on dividend-paying ETFs.

legs.dte_rule: next listed expiry: 1-4 DTE for SPY/QQQ/IWM, 1-7 DTE otherwise

max_profit: Approximately the residual value of the 1-4 DTE long leg at the forced close minus the debit, maximized if spot sits at the strike at exit. Realistically 15-35% of the debit.
max_loss: The net debit paid; in practice capped much tighter by the forced exit, because the long leg still holds one or more days of extrinsic when you close.
breakevens: Intraday, not at expiry. Roughly strike +/- (0.8 to 1.2) x the debit in underlying points at the 14:30 ET exit, computed with the back leg's IV.

greeks.delta: ~0 at ATM entry, but swings fast - 0DTE gamma dominates
greeks.gamma: sharply negative and accelerating into the close; the dominant risk
greeks.theta: strongly positive for the first half of the session, then overwhelmed by gamma
greeks.vega: positive but small - the back leg is only days out

when_to_use: Only on SPY, QQQ or IWM where daily expiries exist, on a quiet, non-trending session: opening range < 0.6% and VIX < 20. Strongly prefer days with no FOMC, CPI, NFP, or major earnings after-hours. This structure is short gamma on the most gamma-heavy instrument in the market; it is a small-size, high-discipline trade.
entry_rules: Underlying limited to SPY, QQQ, IWM (daily expiries, penny-wide markets, share-settled - so assignment discipline is mandatory).
Entry window 10:00-12:30 ET only. Never in the first 30 minutes (opening gamma) and never after 12:30 (no time left to be right).
No macro release (FOMC statement, CPI, PPI, NFP, PCE) scheduled for that session.
VIX < 20 AND the first-30-minute range < 0.6% of spot.
Short strike by delta 0.30-0.50 and at least 0.5 x the 5-minute ATR(14) away from spot.
Net debit <= $0.60 per unit, and total 0DTE calendar debit <= 0.5% of equity per session ($250 on $50k).
Bid-ask on the 2-leg package <= $0.05; reject anything wider.
Max 3 units per session; no re-entry after two stop-outs in the same session.

LEVEL 3 OK (same strike, long expires later). Single mleg order. Alpaca note: verify the mleg fills as a package - if it does not, do NOT leg into a 0DTE short first; fill the long leg first or skip the trade.
management_rules: Profit target +20% of debit, or $0.10 per unit, whichever comes first.
Stop at -40% of debit, or if spot trades through the short strike by more than 0.3 x ATR(5min).
Absolute time stop: 14:00 ET - if not at target, begin working the close.
No rolling. A 0DTE short is never rolled into the same session; it is closed.
Hard daily loss cap: stop trading day calendars for the session after -1% of equity in this bucket.
exit_rules: HARD RULE: the 0DTE short leg must be closed by 14:30 ET, every session, regardless of P&L or moneyness. No exceptions, no discretion, no 'it will come back'.
If the short is ITM at any point after 13:30 ET, close it immediately - do not wait for 14:30.
Close the short leg first, then decide whether to keep the 1-4 DTE long as a lottery ticket (default: close it too, same order).
If the spread mark goes to zero bid on the short, buy it back for $0.01-$0.02 and book the gain.
Never allow a 0DTE short to reach 15:55 ET. SPY/QQQ/IWM settle in shares; an ITM short at the bell means 100 shares delivered against you over the weekend or overnight.
assignment_risk: Maximum in this family. The 0DTE short on a share-settled ETF can be assigned at expiry (automatic exercise if $0.01 ITM) delivering 100 shares long or short per contract. The long 1-4 DTE leg covers directionally but not operationally - you still wake up with an unwanted equity position and overnight gap risk. The 14:30 ET forced close is the only real defense and must be enforced by the automation, not by a human.
buying_power: Net debit only while both legs are open. An assignment converts it into a stock position with a full margin requirement overnight - which is exactly what the 14:30 rule exists to prevent.
liquidity_needs: SPY/QQQ/IWM only: penny-wide 0DTE ATM quotes, OI >= 5,000 on the short strike, and a quoted back-leg spread <= $0.03. Do not run this on single stocks.
common_mistakes: Running it on a trend day (short gamma bleeds continuously); entering too late in the session; sizing it like a normal calendar; holding past 14:30 'because it is almost back to even'; assuming a 0DTE ETF option is cash-settled - it is not, SPY/QQQ/IWM deliver shares (only index products like SPX are cash-settled, and this account trades equities/ETFs).
zero_dte_notes: This IS the 0DTE variant of the family. The whole strategy is defined by the forced 14:30 ET close. A 0DTE double calendar (put day-calendar below and call day-calendar above) is the natural extension: same rules, half the size per side, same forced close.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
